$comment: Advisories the mobile CI audit gate (scripts/audit-gate.mjs --dir packages/mobile --omit-dev, run from .github/workflows/mobile.yml) tolerates. Same rules as the root .audit-allowlist.json: each entry MUST carry a justification and a reviewBy date; the gate warns (does not fail) past reviewBy so releases can't be broken by a calendar. Remove an entry the moment a fix ships. This file is separate from the root one because packages/mobile vendors its own package-lock.json and its exposure analysis is its own.

allow.title: image-size ICNS parser allows denial of service through an infinite loop
allow.justification: NO PATCHED RELEASE EXISTS: the advisory range is <=2.0.2 with first_patched_version null, and 2.0.2 is the newest published version (dist-tags.latest), so neither a bump nor an override can resolve it. The vulnerable copy is image-size@1.2.1, pinned transitively by react-native@0.85.3 -> @react-native/community-cli-plugin -> metro@0.84.4; it is reachable only through that chain, never imported by app code (no reference anywhere in packages/mobile/src). Exposure: NIL at runtime. metro is the React Native BUNDLER — it runs on a developer machine or the EAS builder, not on device; the shipped app executes a pre-built JS bundle that contains no metro and no image-size. It appears under --omit=dev only because react-native declares community-cli-plugin as a production dependency, a packaging artifact rather than shipped runtime code. The DoS requires parsing a malformed ICNS image, and the only images metro reads are the first-party assets committed in this repo, so the worst case is a hung local or EAS build triggered by an asset we authored. Re-check when metro drops image-size or image-size ships a fixed release.

allow.title: image-size JXL and HEIF parsers allow denial of service through infinite loops
allow.justification: Same unpatched image-size@1.2.1 via react-native -> @react-native/community-cli-plugin -> metro, and the same build-time-only exposure as GHSA-w3rx-r6r6-pgpr (no patched release below or above 2.0.2; metro never ships to the device; only first-party committed assets are parsed). The affected parsers are JXL and HEIF, neither of which is an asset format used by this app.

allow.title: decode-uri-component denial of service via exponential decoding of malformed percent-encoded input
allow.justification: NO VIABLE FIX IN THIS TREE. The vulnerable copy is decode-uri-component@0.2.2, pinned transitively by expo-router@56.2.10 -> query-string@7.1.3. Three routes were checked and all break the app: (1) npm's own suggested fix is expo-router@5.1.11, which is a MAJOR DOWNGRADE from the installed 56.2.10 and would gut the router entirely; (2) overriding decode-uri-component to a patched release is impossible because every version above the <=0.4.2 advisory range is ESM-only (0.4.1 and 0.5.0 both declare type=module) while query-string@7.1.3 is CommonJS and require()s it, so the override would fail at runtime with ERR_REQUIRE_ESM; (3) overriding query-string to 9.x hits the same wall, as it is also type=module. The newest expo-router in the 56 line (56.2.20) still declares query-string@^7.1.3, so waiting for a patch release does not help either. EXPOSURE: low but not nil, and worth stating precisely. Scanned QR payloads do NOT reach this code -- src/app/scan-qr.tsx parses them with its own regex plus the native global decodeURIComponent (parseFilamentDeepLink), never query-string. The reachable path is the OS-delivered deep link: app.json declares scheme 'filamentdb', so a hostile filamentdb:// URL opened from a web page or another app is parsed by expo-router via query-string. The impact is a hang of the user's own app on their own device, recoverable by force-quitting; there is no server component and no data disclosure. Re-check when expo-router moves off query-string@7 or query-string ships a CommonJS build with a patched decoder.

allow.title: Zod can exhaust memory while validating oversized constrained collections
allow.justification: NO PATCH WITHIN ZOD 3: the advisory covers zod <4.6.6 and its only fixed release is 4.6.6 on the zod 4 major, while the installed copy, zod@3.25.76, is the newest zod 3 on the registry. The copy is required as zod ^3.25.76 by the Expo CLI (expo/node_modules/@expo/cli@56.1.15) and is shared with eslint-plugin-react-hooks (^3.25.0 || ^4.0.0, via eslint-config-expo). Even the newest @expo/cli (58.1.15) still declares zod ^3.25.76, so no Expo upgrade helps, and an override to zod 4 would hand the CLI a breaking major under the bare 'zod' import it calls with the zod 3 API. Exposure: NIL on device. The Expo CLI validates dev-tools plugin manifests and CLI-extension command output with zod while 'expo start' runs on the developer machine or the EAS builder, and the lint plugin validates its own ESLint options; neither ships in the app bundle (packages/mobile/src never imports zod), and the inputs are the project's own installed packages and config, not untrusted data. It shows under --omit=dev only because expo and eslint-config-expo are declared as production dependencies. Re-check when @expo/cli moves to zod 4.6.6 or later.

allow.title: decode-uri-component denial of service via quadratic replacement of percent-encoded runs
allow.justification: NO VIABLE FIX IN THIS TREE, for the same reason as GHSA-vcc3-ghjq-m6fr above. The advisory covers decode-uri-component <=0.5.0 and its only fixed release is 0.5.1, which declares type=module. The installed copy is decode-uri-component@0.2.2, required (^0.2.2) by query-string@7.1.3, which is CommonJS and require()s it, so an override to 0.5.1 would fail at runtime with ERR_REQUIRE_ESM. query-string@7.1.3 is in turn required (^7.1.3) by expo-router@56.2.10. npm's suggested fix is expo-router@58.0.31, a semver-major move that belongs to an Expo SDK upgrade (this app is on expo ~56), not a dependency bump. EXPOSURE: the same path as the existing entry, low but not nil. Scanned QR payloads do not reach this code (src/app/scan-qr.tsx parses them with its own regex and the native decodeURIComponent). The reachable input is an OS-delivered filamentdb:// deep link, which expo-router parses via query-string; a hostile link with many malformed percent-encoded runs can hang the user's own app on their own device, recoverable by force-quitting. There is no server component and no data disclosure. Re-check at the next Expo SDK upgrade, or when query-string ships a CommonJS build with a patched decoder.

allow.title: glob AbortSignal cancellation bypass allows post-timeout filesystem traversal
allow.justification: NO PATCH WITHIN GLOB 13: the advisory covers glob >=9.0.0 <=14.0.1 and its only fixed release is 14.0.2 on the next major, while the installed copy is glob@13.0.6 and the newest glob 13 on the registry, 13.0.7, is still inside the range (the gate was re-run against it). It is required as ^13.0.0 by Expo's build tooling only: @expo/config@56.0.9, @expo/config-plugins@56.0.8, @expo/fingerprint@0.19.4, @expo/metro-config@56.0.14 and the Expo CLI (expo/node_modules/@expo/cli@56.1.15). An override to glob 14 would hand all five a new major under a ^13 range, and glob 14 itself moves to minimatch ^11 and path-scurry ^3; that cannot be verified here without running the Expo toolchain end to end. Exposure: NIL on device. The flaw is that an aborted async walk keeps reading directories after the caller's AbortSignal fired, which matters to a service that uses a signal or timeout to bound the cost of globbing attacker-influenced patterns. Here glob runs inside expo start/export/prebuild and Metro on a developer machine or the EAS builder, over the project's own tree with patterns from the project's own config; nothing in packages/mobile/src imports glob and none of it is bundled into the app. The worst case is extra filesystem work in a local or EAS build. It shows under --omit=dev only because expo declares its CLI and config packages as production dependencies. Re-check when Expo's tooling moves to glob 14.0.2 or later.

allow.title: minimatch potential denial of service via globparts amplification
allow.justification: NO PATCH WITHIN MINIMATCH 10: the advisory covers minimatch >=7.0.0 <11.0.1 and its only fixed release is 11.0.1 on the next major, while the installed copy is minimatch@10.2.5 and the newest minimatch 10 on the registry, 10.2.6, is still inside the range (the advisory itself was demonstrated against 10.2.6). It is required as ^10.2.2 by glob@13.0.6 (see GHSA-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4), @expo/fingerprint@0.19.4 and @typescript-eslint/typescript-estree@8.61.0 (via eslint-config-expo). An override to minimatch 11 would give all three a new major under a ^10 range, and minimatch 11 also drops Node 18. The other minimatch copies in the tree are 3.1.5, outside the advisory range. Exposure: NIL on device. The denial of service needs an attacker-supplied glob PATTERN; every pattern reaching this copy comes from the project's own configuration (Expo fingerprint and config globs, tsconfig include/exclude read by the lint parser) on a developer machine or the EAS builder. Nothing in packages/mobile/src imports minimatch and none of it ships in the app bundle. It shows under --omit=dev only because expo and eslint-config-expo are declared as production dependencies. Re-check when glob 13's dependents and @expo/fingerprint move to minimatch 11.0.1 or later.
